processes.title: Classic Intercompany Sales
processes.memory_hook: One company sells; another company delivers and bills internally.
processes.business_intent: Serve an external customer from a plant belonging to another company code while keeping customer billing and internal intercompany billing separate.

control_plane.control: company code of sales area vs delivering plant

control_plane.why: enables the delivering company to bill the selling company

data_hinges.changes: customer ownership and internal customer relationship
internal transfer price, not external customer price

impact_summary: The customer sees one seller, while accounting sees two legal entities and two commercial relationships.
constraints: Classic intercompany is a different solution from advanced intercompany.
Internal master-data assignments and billing setup are mandatory.
Deployment and local legal requirements can change the exact scope.
lead_questions: Which legal entity owns the customer contract?
Should this remain classic or move to advanced intercompany?

processes.title: Advanced Intercompany Sales
processes.memory_hook: Cross-company sales becomes an orchestrated value chain.

sap_scope_items.label: Advanced Intercompany Sales – MTO and Variant Configuration

processes.business_intent: Orchestrate a cross-company customer sale with generated intercompany purchasing and sales documents, valuated stock in transit, invoice verification, and value-chain monitoring.

control_plane.control: delivering plant in another company code

control_plane.why: represents control of goods between legal entities

control_plane.control: independent pricing in selling and delivering companies
control_plane.why: separates external and internal commercial logic

data_hinges.changes: company code, generated intercompany documents and transit context
VSiT and timing of ownership/control transfer
whether generated procurement documents can be created
whether advanced MTO/AVC or sales-kit constraints apply

impact_summary: Adds procurement, intercompany sales, internal billing, invoice verification and stock-in-transit events to what externally still looks like one customer order.
constraints: Some advanced combinations need additional scope items, for example MTO/AVC or sales-kit support.
Substitution, TM, compliance and industry overlays have scenario-specific boundaries.
lead_questions: Why do we need AIC rather than classic intercompany?
Which document is leading when a generated document disagrees?
At which event does each company recognize inventory and margin?
How do we monitor broken orchestration?

processes.title: Sell from Stock with Valuated Stock in Transit
processes.memory_hook: Goods left the plant, but we still own/control them.

sap_scope_items.label: Sell from Stock with Valuated Stock in Transit

processes.business_intent: Separate physical goods issue from transfer of control so inventory remains valuated while goods are in transit.

control_plane.why: decide which sales items use the VSiT value chain
maps document/item context to VSiT steps
separates physical departure from ownership/control transfer
posts into and out of VSiT

data_hinges.changes: when VSiT leaves the company's valuated stock

impact_summary: Inventory valuation can remain with the seller after physical PGI; that changes period-end inventory and revenue/cost timing assumptions.
constraints: You cannot freely switch a partially delivered relevant item between standard SFS and VSiT.
Exact relevance criteria and movement mappings are configuration-sensitive.
lead_questions: Is physical GI being mistaken for legal/economic transfer?
Which Incoterm assumption drives the accounting design?
